durability_constraint: A forecast surplus is not a recurring post-shock flow; any realized cushion appears through starting inventories, spare production, or lower required output.
source_note: IEA's June retrospective says its February balances indicated a 3.7 mb/d 2026 surplus before the war.
double_counting_note: Do not add 3.7 mb/d to observed stock draws or incremental supply. It is the prewar balance condition and was partly embodied in stocks already accumulated.
interpretation: Use as context and counterfactual sensitivity rather than a cumulative pie slice.

durability_constraint: Finite one-time inventory cushion; availability varies by location, ownership, product, and operational minimum.
source_note: IEA reported a 477 mb global observed stock build in 2025, equal to 1.3 mb/d on average.
double_counting_note: This is a pre-conflict stock accumulation, not a post-February 2026 market supply flow. Do not add it to postwar observed draws.
interpretation: Supports the claim that the system entered the shock with unusually large aggregate stocks.

durability_constraint: Only part is discretionary: location, ownership, crude/product mix, sanctions, and minimum operating stocks constrain drawability.
source_note: IEA assessed more than 8.2 billion barrels of observed global crude and product inventories, the highest since February 2021.
double_counting_note: Stock level is not supply delivered and must not be added to subsequent stock draws.
interpretation: Use to size the gross stock base, not the amount actually available to offset the disruption.

durability_constraint: Sustainable only within demonstrated pipeline, terminal, security, maintenance, and destination constraints; not indefinitely expandable.
source_note: IEA said early-April alternative-route exports rose to 7.2 mb/d from less than 4 mb/d before the war.
double_counting_note: This is actual Gulf export preservation, already reflected in actual Gulf/global supply. Do not also count it as non-Gulf replacement or add the full 7.2 mb/d as an increment.
interpretation: The incremental route contribution is at least roughly 3.2 mb/d versus the stated prewar upper bound but should be reconciled in the physical Gulf panel.

durability_constraint: A continuing flow, but bounded by East-West pipeline throughput, Yanbu terminal operations, Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb security, crude availability, and maintenance.
source_note: IEA reported Yanbu exports above 5 mb/d in early June versus 2 mb/d before the war.
double_counting_note: Count only the increment versus the frozen counterfactual. Overseas Saudi stock deliveries mentioned by IEA are inventory draw, not pipeline production.
interpretation: Strong evidence that Saudi bypass use rose by more than 3 mb/d at the early-June peak.

durability_constraint: Capacity is durable infrastructure but actual use may be lower and is constrained by field, terminal, storage, and maintenance conditions.
source_note: IEA says the Habshan-Fujairah pipeline enables 1.8 mb/d of crude exports bypassing Hormuz.
double_counting_note: Capacity is not observed incremental flow. Do not add 1.8 mb/d to UAE total exports or to the 7.2 mb/d Gulf alternative-route total.
interpretation: Scenario ceiling/corroboration only unless actual monthly pipeline loadings are available.

durability_constraint: Includes pipeline, storage, and limited/dark Hormuz or Omani-coast movements; durability depends on security and finite stocks.
source_note: IEA reported UAE exports at 4.3 mb/d in early June, up from 1.9 mb/d in March and about 85% of prewar levels.
double_counting_note: Total exports mix bypass, limited transit, production, and stock draw. Do not allocate the whole total to bypass or incremental production.
interpretation: Useful for the realized physical-flow panel; channel attribution requires subtraction of baseline route flows and inventory releases.

durability_constraint: June included a temporary reopening and release of stranded/onshore barrels; it is not automatically a sustainable current-traffic assumption.
source_note: IEA reported June Gulf exports of 16.1 mb/d, up 6.5 mb/d month on month but below the 24 mb/d prewar average.
double_counting_note: The 6.5 mb/d rebound combines renewed Strait traffic, bypasses, and inventory draw; Gulf production rose only 3.5 mb/d. Do not count the export rebound again as production or stock supply.
interpretation: Best June historical anchor for the physical Gulf-flow side of the bridge.

durability_constraint: Renewed hostilities and threats to Bab el-Mandeb make late-June flows an insecure ceiling; current traffic should be set from the refreshed tanker series.
source_note: IEA said July Gulf exports were below late-June highs but still considerably above early-March to mid-June levels.
double_counting_note: Do not infer a numeric July mb/d rate from this qualitative statement.
interpretation: Use only as a cross-check on the sibling tanker-derived current-traffic scenario.

durability_constraint: Production gains can persist if wells, projects, takeaway, and export capacity sustain them; this is a forecast revision, not a monthly observed response.
source_note: IEA said expected 2026 Americas supply growth had been revised up by more than 0.6 mb/d since the start of the year, to 1.5 mb/d.
double_counting_note: Only the revision relative to the frozen prewar counterfactual is potentially additional. The full 1.5 mb/d includes growth already forecast before the shock.
interpretation: Best public quantitative bound for incremental non-Gulf production, pending a February-vintage country panel.

geography: Atlantic Basin to East of Suez
durability_constraint: Trade redirection can continue while arbitrage, tanker, port, crude-quality, and destination-refinery constraints permit; it is not new supply by itself.
source_note: IEA reported Atlantic Basin crude exports up 3.5 mb/d since February, with gains from the United States, Brazil, Canada, Kazakhstan, and Venezuela.
double_counting_note: This mixes higher production, redirection of existing exports, and possibly stock draw. Do not use 3.5 mb/d as an incremental-production slice.
interpretation: Evidence of replacement geography; classify as redirection unless a production delta versus February forecast is separately identified.

durability_constraint: Export gains are constrained by production, refinery output, domestic stock minima, port capacity, and foreign demand.
source_note: IEA reported a record 13.1 mb/d of US crude and product exports in May, nearly one-quarter above a year earlier.
double_counting_note: Exports were supported by higher production plus industry and government stock draw; they are not a pure production response and may redirect barrels from other buyers.
interpretation: Useful destination-flow evidence but not directly pie-additive.

durability_constraint: One-time policy envelope released on country-specific schedules; availability is not the same as barrels already delivered.
source_note: IEA members unanimously agreed to make 400 mb available.
double_counting_note: Do not count announced availability as observed supply. Later provisional country contributions sum to 426 mb and include 28 mb of production rather than stocks.
interpretation: Use the actual cumulative-release row for the pie; retain this row for program scale.

durability_constraint: Finite government-controlled stocks; detailed split was explicitly provisional and country implementation varies.
source_note: IEA's provisional 426 mb country table assigned 280 mb to public stocks.
double_counting_note: Included within the provisional 426 mb total and largely within subsequent actual releases; do not add to them.
interpretation: Separates public stocks from obligated-industry relief and production.

durability_constraint: Drawability depends on national minimum-stock rules and operating needs; obligation relief is not proof all barrels left tanks.
source_note: IEA's provisional table assigned 119 mb to obligated industry stocks.
double_counting_note: Do not label this government SPR or ordinary commercial draw. It is included within the provisional action total and may overlap observed OECD industry-stock changes.
interpretation: Keep as a distinct stock-ownership class in the ledger.

durability_constraint: A flow contribution rather than inventory; durability depends on the producing assets and export logistics.
source_note: IEA's provisional table included 23.6 mb from Canada and 3.9 mb from Mexico, rounded to 28 mb total, as production increases.
double_counting_note: Do not include this volume in government or industry stock release. It may overlap the Americas production-revision row.
interpretation: Reconcile with the February-vintage non-Gulf production counterfactual before counting.

durability_constraint: Short-term release rate; cannot continue indefinitely and varied during the ramp-up.
source_note: IEA said the collective action was bringing 2.5 mb/d to market in May.
double_counting_note: This is contained in observed government/obligated stock declines and the later 290 mb cumulative release. Do not add both rate and volume.
interpretation: Use monthly only if reconstructing timing; use the cumulative actual for an as-of-July pie.

durability_constraint: Finite; more of the original action was still flowing, but releases draw down emergency buffers and depend on policy decisions.
source_note: IEA reported around 290 mb released since the 11 March announcement.
double_counting_note: Actual cumulative program figure may include public and obligated-industry barrels; do not add provisional components or observed total-stock draws without ownership reconciliation.
interpretation: Best as-of-July cumulative strategic/emergency-release anchor.

durability_constraint: Gross remaining stocks are not all releasable: 90-day commitments, national law, product/location mismatch, drawdown rates, and operational floors apply.
source_note: IEA said members still held over 1 billion barrels of government-controlled stocks.
double_counting_note: A stock level is not future flow and should not be added to actual releases.
interpretation: Useful gross durability bound; future scenarios need a policy/operationally usable subset and release-rate limit.

durability_constraint: Rapid draws cannot persist at the same pace as working inventories approach operational minima; revisions are material.
source_note: June OMR estimated a 3.8 mb/d average global stock draw since the war began, split 2.4 crude and 1.4 products.
double_counting_note: Includes government, obligated, commercial, non-OECD visible stocks, and oil-on-water movements. Do not add its components or emergency releases on top.
interpretation: Superseded for cumulative charting where later monthly revisions are available; retain as a vintage marker.

durability_constraint: June's net build was dominated by oil on water and can reverse as cargoes discharge; onshore tanks continued drawing.
source_note: IEA said global observed stocks rose 21 mb in June, the first monthly build since the war began.
double_counting_note: Net total already combines +117 mb oil on water and about -96 mb onshore; do not add those components separately.
interpretation: Use +21 mb as the June net stock-flow term, with sign convention made explicit in the bridge.

durability_constraint: Mostly a timing/location buffer; stranded or sailing barrels are not necessarily available to end users until discharged and can unwind quickly.
source_note: IEA reported oil on water swelled by 117 mb in June.
double_counting_note: Component of the +21 mb global net stock change and linked to the Gulf export surge; do not count as new supply or an additional stock cushion.
interpretation: Keep visible in the audit waterfall to explain why global stocks built while onshore stocks fell.

durability_constraint: Working stocks have operational minima and heterogeneous ownership; sustained draws must taper.
source_note: IEA reported continued onshore draws of about 96 mb in June.
double_counting_note: Component of the +21 mb global net stock change; includes the 44 mb OECD government draw and other onshore categories.
interpretation: Use subcomponents only when the ownership ledger is reconciled; otherwise use the net global stock change.

durability_constraint: Finite emergency stocks and policy schedules constrain continuation.
source_note: IEA estimated 44 mb of June's 62 mb OECD stock decline came from government releases.
double_counting_note: Subset of OECD, onshore, and global stock changes; also part of the 290 mb cumulative IEA release. Count only once.
interpretation: Useful monthly ownership split but cumulative chart should reconcile to the 290 mb program total or a complete monthly ledger.

durability_constraint: Shows China initially kept building; location and ownership remain opaque.
source_note: IEA reported China added 40 mb of crude to tanks in March.
double_counting_note: Part of global/non-OECD observed stocks; not evidence of SPR release.
interpretation: Important chronology against claims that China immediately launched a massive government-SPR draw.

durability_constraint: Large June draw may include commercial, operational, government-directed commercial, bonded, or other barrels; ownership is not observable.
source_note: IEA said China led the non-OECD crude-stock decline with a 41 mb draw in June.
double_counting_note: Subset of non-OECD and global stock changes. Do not count it separately from the global net stock term unless decomposing ownership.
interpretation: Best official/agency monthly evidence for a large China draw, but not for a government SPR draw.

durability_constraint: Opaque and not a public Chinese series; legal and operational release limits are unknown.
source_note: EIA estimated about 360 mb of government-held Chinese crude in December 2025.
double_counting_note: A stock level is not an observed draw and is separate from EIA's estimated 1 billion barrels of commercial crude.
interpretation: Use only as a rough scenario durability stock base with wide uncertainty.

durability_constraint: Only a fraction is discretionary above working minima; EIA treats China commercial stocks as strategically directed, but they are not a government SPR.
source_note: EIA estimated about 1 billion barrels of Chinese commercial crude inventories in December 2025.
double_counting_note: Do not add the 1.0 bn commercial estimate to EIA's 1.4 bn broad China strategic estimate; the latter includes commercial stocks.
interpretation: Supports a large commercial/operational cushion while preserving ownership ambiguity.

durability_constraint: Import cuts can persist only with lower runs/demand, alternative barrels, or continued stock draw; rebound is likely if supply normalizes.
source_note: IEA said China had reduced crude imports by nearly 50% versus prewar levels.
double_counting_note: Import reduction is not an additive global demand-reduction slice: it also reflects stock draw, lower refinery runs, missing Gulf supply, and trade timing.
interpretation: Strong current adjustment signal but requires the national balance to separate stocks from demand.

durability_constraint: Counterfactual only; preserve this vintage for monthly demand-gap calculations.
source_note: IEA forecast 2026 global oil demand growth of 0.85 mb/d before the war.
double_counting_note: Do not add this forecast level to observed demand changes.
interpretation: Frozen benchmark for shock-related demand reduction.

durability_constraint: IEA assumes later-year recovery; a scenario holding current low traffic would need a different demand path.
source_note: IEA projected 2026 demand to fall 1.0 mb/d, after forecasting +0.85 mb/d in February.
double_counting_note: Annual forecast revision is not the realized March-to-latest cumulative gap and overlaps refinery-run, shortage, price, policy, macro, and fuel-switching effects.
interpretation: Implies a 1.85 mb/d downward revision versus the frozen annual-growth forecast, but monthly bridge values should come from the balance task.

durability_constraint: Much is temporary or involuntary and may rebound with product availability; persistence differs by sector.
source_note: IEA estimated a 4.8 mb/d year-on-year demand contraction in 2Q26.
double_counting_note: Year-on-year change is not the same as change versus the frozen February monthly forecast. Do not add refinery-run cuts separately.
interpretation: Strong realized-quarter anchor; convert to the frozen-counterfactual basis before pie use.

durability_constraint: May was the nadir; July OMR expected a rebound as products and seasonal activity recovered.
source_note: IEA put May demand at 97.9 mb/d, down 5.3 mb/d year on year.
double_counting_note: Level must be compared with the February monthly forecast, not directly added to a year-on-year change.
interpretation: Best latest-vintage monthly demand anchor in the public IEA summary.

durability_constraint: EIA assumes demand rebounds in 2027 after prices, shortages, and policy restraint ease.
source_note: EIA forecast 2026 consumption down 1.2 mb/d, with 0.8 mb/d of the decline in non-OECD countries.
double_counting_note: Independent balance check, not additive to IEA's demand estimate.
interpretation: Use as model sensitivity around IEA rather than combine the two agencies.

durability_constraint: EIA expects the draw to moderate to 2.2 mb/d in 3Q under its reopening forecast; a fixed-low-traffic scenario invalidates that assumption.
source_note: EIA estimated global oil inventories fell 5.1 mb/d on average in 2Q26.
double_counting_note: Independent model-balance estimate; do not average or add to IEA observed-stock estimates.
interpretation: Useful high-side/sensitivity check because it is a modeled total balance rather than the IEA observed-inventory ledger.

durability_constraint: Run cuts are reversible and partly forced by feedstock shortages; restarting depends on crude/product flows and refinery condition.
source_note: IEA reported refinery crude runs in China, the Middle East, Eurasia, and elsewhere in Asia down by more than 5 mb/d year on year in 2Q26.
double_counting_note: A refinery-run cut is a transmission mechanism from crude shortage to product supply and end-user demand, not an additional global offset to add beside demand reduction.
interpretation: Keep as explanation and sector allocation evidence, not a pie slice.

durability_constraint: Some efficiency, electrification, and renewable measures may persist, but many policy announcements are temporary and the tracker does not isolate realized oil savings.
source_note: IEA tracks measures across nearly 80 countries and reports fuel switching, renewable scaling, electrification, and conservation actions, but does not publish a de-duplicated realized global oil-displacement total.
double_counting_note: Do not create a separate fuel-switching or renewables slice unless incremental 2026 oil displacement versus the February forecast is measured; it is currently embedded in demand reduction or residual.
interpretation: Narrative subchannel only at this stage.

durability_constraint: Residual uncertainty should widen for forecast months and longer scenarios rather than being forced into named channels.
source_note: Residual equals the accounting gap after using one consistent stock ledger, frozen counterfactual demand and supply, and route-preservation terms.
double_counting_note: Required to absorb statistical discrepancies, timing, revisions, unobserved stocks, and incomplete ownership splits. Never back-allocate mechanically to preferred narratives.
interpretation: Always publish as an explicit slice if material.

durability_constraint: Low holds releases at the 21 July reported total; base extends May's 2.5 mb/d release rate for the final ten days; high allows modestly faster execution but remains below the 400 mb announced envelope.
source_note: IEA reported 290 mb released through 21 July and said more was continuing to flow; the 31 July range is an explicit project estimate, not an IEA figure.
double_counting_note: Alternative to adj-018 for a chart ending 31 July; never add both. It may include public and obligated-industry stocks.
interpretation: Preferred provisional July-end emergency-release range until an official execution update supersedes it.

durability_constraint: Applies EIA's 2.2 mb/d average 3Q draw uniformly to 31 July days; the EIA forecast assumes improving transit and predates the 7-8 July renewed escalation.
source_note: Derived as -2.2 mb/d times 31 days from the July STEO's 3Q inventory-draw forecast; not an observed July stock change.
double_counting_note: Do not combine with an IEA July stock estimate or with component stock-release rows; use only as a sensitivity when closing through 31 July.
interpretation: A low-fidelity July completion proxy that should remain visibly forecast-hatched in charts.
